claim: For every fixed finite \(R\ge2\), there is a dependent triangular array \(\{Y_{i,n}:1\le i\le n,\ n\ge1\}\) with \(\sup_{n,i}\|Y_{i,n}\|_{\Psi_R}<\infty\) and, for every fixed integer \(k\ge1\), \(\operatorname{Var}(n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nY_{i,n}^{k})=O_k(n^{-1})\), but whose empirical measure \(\mu_n=n^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{Y_{i,n}}\) and mean measure \(\bar\mu_n=\mathbb E\mu_n\) satisfy \(\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb E W_1(\mu_n,\bar\mu_n)=\tfrac12W_1(\mu_+,\mu_-)>0\). Here \(\mu_\pm\) have densities \(f_\pm(x)=f(x)[1\pm\sin(2\pi\log x)]\) on \(x>0\), where \(f(x)=(\sqrt{2\pi}x)^{-1}\exp[-(\log x)^2/2]\) is the standard lognormal density. Thus bounded-order \(\Psi_R\) control cannot replace a tail condition whose controlled moment order tends to infinity in a general moment-based empirical-\(W_1\) concentration theorem.

correctness.rationale: The perturbation integral vanishes for every integer \(k\ge0\): it is the imaginary part of \(\exp((k+2\pi i)^2/2)\), whose phase contributes \(\sin(2\pi k)=0\). The resulting densities are distinct and share all moments. Conditional iid sampling gives the law-of-total-variance identity exactly. Conditional empirical \(W_1\) convergence and the one-dimensional CDF representation yield the claimed positive limit.

originality.rationale: The claim is narrowly scoped to an explicit empirical-measure counterexample: bounded-order \(\Psi_R\) control and \(O_k(n^{-1})\) variance of every fixed empirical moment coexist with an exact nonzero limiting expected \(W_1\) gap. Classical moment indeterminacy explains the mechanism, but the inspected sources do not state this exact combined empirical-\(W_1\) boundary result.
residual_risks: The construction is an elementary combination of a classical Stieltjes class, a shared latent selector, and conditional iid convergence; an unindexed prior note may already state this exact specialization.
The result does not establish failure for moment-determinate laws or for assumptions that control tails more strongly than any fixed finite-order Ψ_R norm.
The conclusion relies on unconditional dependence through the shared latent sign.

value.rationale: The result gives a motivated sharpness counterexample to weakening a recent empirical-\(W_1\) concentration theorem's growing-order tail condition: even all fixed empirical moment variances can decay as \(O_k(n^{-1})\), while expected \(W_1\) stays bounded away from zero. The exact limit quantifies the obstruction.
